did.abstract: One bound album of sepia-toned 8x10" photographs of "Shore Acres" on Shore Road, Bay Ridge, circa 1913-1924. The images depict various scenes and views in and around a home and estate in what is now Bay Ridge along Shore Road. The property later became the Shore Road Academy.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This collection consists of a single volume.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: The path along Brooklyn's southwestern coast that became today's Shore Road was used as early as the first years of the 18th century. The area remained part of the town of New Utrecht until that town's incorporation into what was then the city of Brooklyn in 1894. Development in New Utrecht increased steadily throughout the 19th century and the town's population more than quadrupled between 1810 and 1880. By the early 1900s, Shore Road was firmly established as a prime location for the lavish country mansions and estates of New York's wealthiest denizens.

One such denizen was William F. Kenny. Kenny grew up on the Lower East Side of Manhattan. His childhood friend Alfred E. Smith went on to become Governor of New York State and a candidate for President of the United States. Kenny went on to earn millions of dollars with his contracting business and investing. He owned two large mansions along Shore Road: one, on the corner of 91st Street (a property formerly owned by Dr. A. Warner Shepard), later became the Shore Road Hospital, and one, on the corner of Oliver Street, became Shore Road Academy. The latter may also have at one point been home to the Shuttleworth family.

Shore Road Academy was founded in 1924 by Helen Redding and Theodora Goldsmith as "Brooklyn's only country day school for girls." The school operated until 1941. During World War II, the school property was used by the U.S.O. (United Service Organizations). The property was purchased by developers in 1946 and resold in 1949, when it was announced that the building would be demolished in order to build a large apartment building.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: One bound album of sepia-toned 8x10" photographs of "Shore Acres" on Shore Road, Bay Ridge, circa 1913-1924. The images depict various scenes and views in and around a home and estate in what is now Bay Ridge along Shore Road. The property later became the Shore Road Academy. Views include exterior views of the main house from various angles, outbuildings such as chicken coops and greenhouses, a child's playhouse with slide and carousel, and interior views of the mansion's various rooms. The interiors include sitting rooms, bedrooms, bathrooms, a kitchen, wine cellar, children's nursery, painting studio, library, bowling alley, and "rathskeller." There are also three views of steamships passing in the harbor: SS Olympic (first voyage 1911), SS Imperator (first voyage 1913), and SS France (first voyage 1912).
